findings.title: [P2] Detect network requests inside shell command strings
findings.body: A Bash tool input such as `bash -c 'curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xHoneyJar/loa/main/README.md'` bypasses the new egress check. Its program is `bash`, so `egress_command` returns false; the heredoc scanner also finds nothing. An evaluated agent can therefore retrieve upstream content without triggering `network_egress`, defeating the contamination safeguard. Recursively inspect shell `-c` arguments, including `sh -c`, using the same command rules.

findings.description: The class 9 network-egress detector only recognises three literal hosts, and the negative lookbehind `(?<![A-Za-z0-9.-])` in EGRESS_HOST explicitly refuses to match `github.com` when it is preceded by a dot. Every other GitHub subdomain therefore evades the rule, including the hosts that actually serve code: `codeload.github.com` (tarballs/zipballs of any ref), `patch-diff.githubusercontent.com` (the `.diff`/`.patch` of a PR), `gist.github.com` / `gist.githubusercontent.com`, `objects.githubusercontent.com` (release assets) and `www.github.com`. A graded agent running `curl -L https://codeload.github.com/0xHoneyJar/loa/tar.gz/<fix-sha>` or `curl https://patch-diff.githubusercontent.com/raw/0xHoneyJar/loa/pull/1286.diff` is not flagged by egress_command: `host` is False, so the curl/wget branch returns False even though REPO_TOKEN matched. Likewise EGRESS_PYLIB only matches `urllib`/`requests`; `http.client`, `httpx`, `aiohttp`, `pycurl` or raw `socket` code naming github.com in a `python -c` or heredoc body is not seen. Because class 9 was introduced precisely so the KF-046 class 7 PR-content exemption can never excuse a fetch of the repository, a miss here can let the repo-token hit fall back to the exemptable path and the run be graded as clean.
findings.failure_mode: The graded agent downloads the fix (or the whole repository at the fix commit) from a GitHub subdomain, the oracle answer leaks into its review, and the run is scored as uncontaminated; recall and precision statistics for that arm are inflated without any grade.json signal.
findings.suggested_fix: Match any host that ends in `github.com` or `githubusercontent.com` (e.g. `(?<![A-Za-z0-9-])(?:[a-z0-9-]+\.)*(?:github\.com|githubusercontent\.com)(?![A-Za-z0-9-])`) plus `github.io`, and extend EGRESS_PYLIB to `http\.client|httpx|aiohttp|pycurl|socket|urllib3`. Add a bats case for codeload.github.com and patch-diff.githubusercontent.com.

findings.description: egress_command judges a simple command solely by the program in command position after a fixed wrapper list (NAME=value, env, command, exec, nice, timeout). Ordinary shell forms a model naturally emits therefore evade class 9 while naming github.com verbatim: `bash -c 'curl https://github.com/...'` or `sh -c "..."` (only heredoc bodies are recursed into, not `-c` strings); `if curl -fsSL https://github.com/... -o x; then`, `for ...; do curl ...` and `{ curl ...; }` (shell keywords `if`/`do`/`{` land in command position); `time`, `nohup`, `xargs`, `setsid`, `sudo` or `busybox wget` wrappers; `bash <(curl https://github.com/...)` (EGRESS_SUBST only matches `$(` and backticks, not process substitution `<(`); `cat <<EOF | bash` (interpreter_bodies reads the program before the heredoc marker, `cat`, so a body executed by a piped bash is treated as data); and package managers that are themselves fetchers (`pip install git+https://github.com/0xHoneyJar/loa`, `npm i github:0xHoneyJar/loa`, `go get github.com/...`). None of these is covered by the documented lower bound (which names only programs the agent wrote, remotes fetched by name and node/perl/ruby heredocs). Since check_value returns the class 9 verdict before any other class and the class 7 PR-content exemption is designed to apply to the remaining classes, these misses can turn an explicit repository fetch into a clean grade.
findings.failure_mode: A graded agent fetches the fix or repository with a trivially wrapped curl/wget/git invocation that names github.com in the transcript, class 9 reports no hit, and contaminated stays null; the oracle leak is only visible to a human reading the transcript.
findings.suggested_fix: Treat the whole heredoc-stripped segment as egress when it names an EGRESS_HOST together with any of the fetcher tokens (curl, wget, git fetch/clone/pull/ls-remote, gh, pip/npm/go install) anywhere in the segment, not just in command position; recurse into `bash -c`/`sh -c` string arguments and `<(…)`; treat a heredoc whose segment is piped into bash/sh/python as fed to that interpreter; strip leading shell keywords (`if`, `then`, `elif`, `while`, `until`, `do`, `{`, `(`, `!`) and common wrappers (time, nohup, xargs, sudo, setsid, stdbuf) in seg_words. Prefer false positives here: the exemption path still exists for the other classes.

findings.description: The union grader admits a session when cell.json marks it valid and its grade.json has `contaminated: null`, but it never checks the session grade's grader_version or re-runs the contamination scan. A session graded before 1.3.2 (no class 9 at all) or before 1.3.4, or re-graded by an older checkout, carries a null contaminated field even if its transcript shows a github.com fetch; the union then merges its citations into the cell's recall and false_positives and reports `contaminated: null` for the cell. The row writer likewise copies the union grade without checking version agreement across sessions.
findings.failure_mode: A matched cell's union recall includes citations from a session whose egress contamination was never evaluated, and nothing in grade.json or rows.jsonl records the inconsistency.
findings.suggested_fix: In grade_union, require `sg.get("grader_version") == GRADER_VERSION` (or at least a version that includes class 9) for every valid session and raise GradeError otherwise, or re-run the contamination scan over `<run_dir>/transcripts` for each valid session before merging; record per_session[].grader_version in the union grade.

findings.description: The `safe()` filter that sanitises every head-context line, diff line and incident excerpt shown to blind annotators strips C0/C1 controls and the two Unicode line separators, but leaves the bidirectional override and isolate characters (U+202A–U+202E, U+2066–U+2069) and zero-width characters (U+200B–U+200D, U+FEFF) untouched. These are the Trojan Source vectors: a fixture head file or an incident evidence file containing them renders differently from its logical content in a markdown viewer, so an annotator can be shown code that reads as benign (or as changed) while the bytes say otherwise. Fixture head trees are seeded from real PR branches and incident evidence is pulled from repository history, so the content is not under the packet author's control.
findings.failure_mode: An annotator labels a hunk based on a visually misleading rendering, producing a wrong label that then feeds the review-driven and agreement fields of the manifests.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend CTRL to cover `​-‏‪-‮⁠-⁤⁦-⁩﻿` (replace with a visible marker such as `�` rather than a space so the annotator sees that something was removed), and have no-secrets.sh or the leak check refuse a packet that still contains them.
